prompt: Write me a quick script to list all running containers and their ports.
output:
Fish shell, so here's a fish script:

```fish
#!/usr/bin/env fish
docker ps --format "table {{.Names}}\t{{.Ports}}\t{{.Status}}"
```

Or a one-liner if you just want it in the terminal:

```fish
docker ps --format "table {{.Names}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.Ports}}\t{{.Status}}"
```

If you want more detail (host→container port mapping, pretty-printed):

```fish
#!/usr/bin/env fish
for id in (docker ps -q)
    set name (docker inspect --format '{{.Name}}' $id | string trim -c '/')
    set ports (docker port $id)
    echo "=== $name ==="
    if test -n "$ports"
        echo $ports
    else
        echo "(no ports exposed)"
    end
end
```

The `docker ps --format` one-liner is usually enough unless you need the full port mapping detail.
